summary.headline: Vinati Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA fell 27% YoY to INR142 crores on a 21% margin, while net income rose 21% to INR707 crores.
summary.overview: Standalone net income including other income rose 21% YoY to INR707 crores in Q2 FY27, but EBITDA fell 27% to INR142 crores and PAT fell 33% to INR87 crores. Management blamed Middle East war-driven energy and logistics costs that were not fully passed through, plus ATBS volume shifting from Q2 into Q3 and Q4 due to customer destocking. Management guided to 20-25% top-line growth for FY27 and a 24-25% EBITDA margin, with a 25-26% margin targeted for FY28. It also announced two INR500 crore specialty chemical capex plans funded from internal accruals, with the second still at land-acquisition stage.

segments.name: ATBS
segments.commentary: Approximately 27-28% of H1 FY27 sales; demand was weaker than planned in H1 due to customer destocking, with volumes shifting into H2. Management said Q3 shows an uptick in demand.

segments.name: IBB
segments.commentary: Approximately 12-15% of H1 FY27 sales; strong in H1 on both volume and pricing, and management expects similar performance in H2.

segments.name: Butyl Phenols
segments.commentary: Approximately 16-20% of H1 FY27 sales (later restated as 15-17% and 17-18% in the Q&A); described as stable, with better H2 expected.

segments.name: Antioxidants (AO)
segments.commentary: Approximately 15-17% of H1 FY27 sales; strong H1 despite a challenging market, with momentum expected to continue in H2.

segments.name: IB (isobutylene)
segments.commentary: Reported strong H1 performance, with the same expected in H2; no figures were given.

segments.name: VOPL (Veeral Organics)
segments.commentary: Process re-engineering is under way on some products. MEHQ is being self-consumed to make BHA at low volume. Management guided FY27 VOPL revenue of INR75-100 crores, not above INR100 crores, with streamlining expected by April/May 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of 20-25% YoY, driven by volume and pricing.
FY27 EBITDA margin of about 24-25%, down from the earlier 25-30% range.
FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 25-26%; management said the worst is behind us.
Logistics rates began cooling in Q3 FY27, with further reduction expected in Q4, which should help Q3 and Q4 profitability.
VOPL MEHQ and other products to start commercial sales from April 2027; VOPL ramp-up to optimum takes about one year.
capex_capacity: INR500 crore capex for new specialty chemicals for fragrances, personal care, water treatment, oilfields and resins; funded by internal accruals; commercialisation in about two years.
Expected asset turnover of about 1:1 to 1.5x and ROI of 15-20% on the INR500 crore specialty capex.
A second INR500 crore capex plan is at land-acquisition stage, with more clarity in about six months once land and pilot trials are complete; management said it may not proceed.

Products are adjacencies (backward, forward or horizontal) to existing chemistries, tested in pilot trials over the past year; 65-70% expected to be exports; average realisation about USD 3/kg (range USD 2-4.5/kg).
VOPL: five products (MEHQ, guaiacol, anisole, 4-methoxyacetophenone, and isoamylene-based tertiary amyl alcohol, plus PTAP) with revenue starting around December/January.
demand_pricing: Raw material price increases were largely passed on to customers, but energy and logistics cost increases were not fully passed through, which compressed margins.
ATBS demand was hit by customer destocking in H1 and volume is expected to recover in H2, with Q3 seen as strong.
Management said MEHQ demand remains strong because it is used as a polymer inhibitor, and called the current weakness a temporary downturn.
Management said some new products will be the only Indian producer, and that in one segment Vinati would be the second or third producer.

qa_highlights.question: What chemistries are behind the INR500 crore capex, and were they tested in the pilot facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the products are adjacencies to existing chemistries, tested over the last year, and that the company is confident of commercial implementation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q2 margin the lowest in company history?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said ATBS sales shifted from Q2 into Q3 and Q4, which alone cut Q2 margin to 21%, and energy and logistics costs were not fully passed on.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the MEHQ/BHA revenue target of about INR100 crores for this year delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided VOPL FY27 revenue at INR75-100 crores, not above INR100 crores, citing internal re-engineering that should be streamlined by April/May 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 25-26% for FY28, after 24-25% for FY27, and said the worst is behind.

qa_highlights.question: What are the realisations and export share for the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Average realisation about USD 3/kg (range USD 2-4.5/kg); 65-70% of volume expected to be exports.

risks_watch: Energy and logistics cost pass-through: Q3/Q4 relief depends on logistics rates continuing to cool.
VOPL/MEHQ: commercial sales are slipping to April 2027, and the INR100 crore FY27 revenue goal has been cut to INR75-100 crores; competition from China is a concern.
Execution risk on the INR500 crore capex, given management's own admission of past project-execution problems, and a 15-20% ROI target.
ATBS volume recovery in H2 FY27 is not yet confirmed; the Q3 demand upturn is stated, not reported.
Standalone PAT down 33% YoY in Q2; FY27 margin guidance was cut from 25-30% to 24-25%.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on medium-term growth and new capex, but cautious on the near term. It was defensive when pressed on the sharp Q2 margin drop and on VOPL/MEHQ delays, attributing them to timing and internal process fixes. Answers on new-product economics were specific, but some answers were brief or deferred to H2.
key_quotes: You can say the worst is now behind us.
Now the worst is behind us. We can say this thing only.
We expect volume recovery in H2.
It will not cross INR100 crores in this financial year.

growth.why: FY27 top-line guided at 20-25% growth (midpoint ~22.5%) with H1 net income up 25%, backed by ATBS volume shifting into H2, pricing pass-through, and VOPL products from April 2027; however, EBITDA margin guidance was cut to 24-25% from 25-30%, and new INR500 crore capex only commissions in about two years, so the near-term growth is only partially backed by specific capacity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 24-25% (cut from 25-30%) but FY28 guided at 25-26%, with logistics rates cooling from Q3 FY27 and Q2 margin at a 21% low that management attributes mainly to ATBS timing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two INR500 crore specialty plants are announced, but the first only commissions in about two years and the second is still at land-acquisition stage and may not proceed; VOPL products start sales from April 2027 at INR75-100 crore FY27 revenue.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: ATBS volume is shifting from Q2 into Q3/Q4 after customer destocking (ATBS ~27-28% of H1 sales), and FY27 top line is guided at 20-25% growth, though H2 recovery is not yet reported.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: INR500 crore specialty capex is already announced and funded from internal accruals; a second INR500 crore plan is at land-acquisition stage with more clarity in about six months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Margin guidance was cut to 24-25% from 25-30% and VOPL revenue was cut to INR75-100 crore from a ~INR100 crore goal; top-line 20-25% growth is the only firm positive.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Standalone PAT fell 33% YoY in Q2 and energy costs were not fully passed through; delivery of 20-25% top-line growth depends on ATBS H2 recovery and logistics cost relief, neither confirmed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: VOPL MEHQ and other products (five products incl. guaiacol, anisole, PTAP) start commercial sales from April 2027 with revenue starting around December/January; the INR500 crore specialty products commercialise in about two years, with 65-70% expected to be exports at about USD 3/kg.

rows.label: Logistics cost cooling from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Logistics rates began cooling in Q3 FY27 with further reduction expected in Q4, which management says should help Q3 and Q4 profitability after the Q2 energy and logistics squeeze.

rows.label: VOPL process re-engineering streamlined
rows.why: VOPL re-engineering is expected to be streamlined by April/May 2027 and ramp to optimum takes about one year, with MEHQ self-consumed to make BHA at low volume in the meantime.

rows.label: MEHQ demand strength
rows.why: Management says MEHQ demand remains strong as a polymer inhibitor and calls the current weakness temporary, but no volume figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on medium-term growth, FY28 margin of 25-26% and the INR500 crore capex, but cautious and defensive on the near-term Q2 margin drop of 21% and the VOPL/MEHQ revenue cut; analysts pressed on the margin cut and VOPL delays.
